final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral package: 72% RVC phased per platform over three years with binding redesign windows, labor enforcement with automatic tariffs on confirmed violations (60-day audit trigger, no Mexican discretion), five-year review mechanism replacing hard sunset, Chapter 19 preserved, and Canada conceding 50K metric tons fluid milk + 20K cheese quotas to secure U.S. agriculture support for ratification.
minority_objections: Dairy_ag initially resisted closing without concrete agricultural market access beyond supply-chain theory
Auto_industry raised operational feasibility concerns about calendar-hard RVC deadlines before per-platform compromise
key_conflicts: Canada's dairy supply management vs. U.S. agriculture demand for market access (resolved via limited quota concession)
Mexico's sovereignty over audit process vs. Congress/labor demand for automatic enforcement without discretion
Auto industry's need for platform-specific phase-in vs. USTR's initial calendar-hard RVC deadline
Sunset clause business uncertainty vs. need for agreement stability (resolved via review mechanism)
key_concessions: Mexico accepted independent audits with automatic tariff penalties on confirmed labor violations, no discretion to waive
Canada conceded 50K metric tons fluid milk and 20K cheese quotas over three years despite dairy being initial red line
USTR shifted from calendar-hard 72% RVC to per-platform phase-in tied to actual redesign cycles
All parties accepted five-year review with mutual termination rights instead of hard sunset
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement mechanism non-negotiable (held throughout)
Canada: Dairy supply management core protection (partially breached via quota concession)
Congress/Labor: Labor enforcement must include automatic penalties, not discretionary committees
Mexico: Audits conducted under Mexican law, not U.S. inspectors with blank check (held)
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Compliance cost and supplier reorganization burden during three-year phase-in received acknowledgment but no mitigation mechanism beyond cure windows
Political ratification risk in Canada from dairy quota concession was noted but not fully explored
Enforcement verification mechanism details (who confirms redesign windows, audit quality standards) deferred to legal drafting
downstream_risk_variables: Whether OEMs actually commit binding redesign windows in legal text or retain flexibility
Canadian Cabinet and dairy farmer reaction to 50K/20K quota concession
Congressional agriculture caucus acceptance of quota numbers as sufficient market access
Implementation of automatic tariff penalties without creating trade war escalation
Audit quality and independence under Mexican law in practice
uncertainty_notes: Legal text must still lock binding OEM redesign window commitments to prevent slippage loopholes. Canadian Cabinet verbal commitment to dairy quotas requires formal ratification. Audit quality standards and verification procedures for labor enforcement deferred to implementation. Supply chain adjustment costs acknowledged but not quantified or mitigated beyond fiscal year-end reconciliation windows.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 72% RVC and per-platform phase-in drove multiple rounds of negotiation, forced USTR to abandon calendar-hard deadline, and was explicitly cited by auto_industry as investment-freeze trigger requiring resolution before signature
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Independent audits with automatic tariff penalties became the core enforcement compromise that unlocked Mexico's acceptance and Congress's ratification commitment; Congress stated 'binational committees won't fly on the Hill' and made automatic penalties a voting condition
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Canada's initial 'supply management not negotiable' red line was breached via 50K/20K quota concession explicitly to secure U.S. agriculture support and Congressional ratification; dairy_ag stated 'Congress votes no' without it
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated 'Chapter 19 non-negotiable, full stop' in opening and it was preserved throughout, but it did not drive any specific proposal or concession—simply held as background constraint
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Five-year review mechanism replaced hard sunset to address business uncertainty raised by supply_chain_mfr, but the compromise was accepted quickly without extended negotiation or blocking the deal
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress explicitly conditioned votes on labor enforcement text, dairy quotas, and auto phase-in clarity; us_congress stated 'deal dies on the Hill' multiple times, directly shaping USTR's enforcement and agriculture concessions
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Supply_chain_mfr and auto_industry raised compliance costs and sourcing reorganization concerns repeatedly, but these were acknowledged via cure windows and phase-in flexibility rather than driving new proposals
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: Mexico's 'sign now or watch this package collapse' and 'we walk to legal right now' ultimatums explicitly pressured Canada to accept 72% RVC and dairy quotas; mexico_neg stated 'Canada walks in now or we move without them'
